chunks.text:
[building] Town Center (Sci-Fi mode name: Command Center)
cost: free; health 800; population +25; trains Worker
Starting building. Trains Workers, is the drop-off point for gathered resources and gives +25 population capacity. If your Town Center is destroyed you lose the match.

[building] House (Sci-Fi mode name: Habitat)
cost: 30 wood; health 150; population +5
Cheap building that raises the population cap by +5. Build Houses before the population limit blocks unit training.

[building] Barracks (Sci-Fi mode name: Armory)
cost: 100 wood; health 400; trains Spearman, Archer
Military building required to train Spearmen and Archers (Marines and Snipers in Sci-Fi). Training queue holds up to 5 units.

[building] Stable (Sci-Fi mode name: Vehicle Bay)
cost: 120 wood, 20 gold; health 450; trains Cavalry
Required to train Cavalry (Tanks in Sci-Fi). Training queue holds up to 5 units.

[building] Blacksmith (Sci-Fi mode name: Tech Lab)
cost: 120 wood, 40 gold; health 450
Research building. All Weapon, Armor and Wall upgrades are researched here, one research at a time. If it is destroyed during research, the research is cancelled and refunded.

[building] Mine (Sci-Fi mode name: Gold Refinery)
cost: 75 gold; health 500
Gold-only building (75 gold, 2x2) that produces +10 gold every 10 seconds while one Worker is assigned inside it (max 1 worker). It does not need a gold node: it can be placed on any explored, open 2x2 ground. The worker inside is hidden and cannot be attacked. Build it when gold income is low.

[building] Archer Tower (Sci-Fi mode name: Rocket Turret)
cost: 100 gold; health 450
Defensive tower (100 gold, 2x2). It must be manned by one soldier to fire: an Archer in Medieval, a Marine or Sniper in Sci-Fi. Archer Tower: 12 damage, range 6.5, every 1.6 s. Rocket Turret: 30 damage, range 7, every 3 s. Only Archers can damage an enemy Archer Tower and only Tanks can damage an enemy Rocket Turret. Place it on the side attacks come from or next to mines and farms.

[building] Wall
cost: 10 wood; health 300
1x1 wall segment, 10 wood each (5 s to build), drawn by dragging. Walls block movement, so leave a gap/gate for your own units and keep resource paths open. Health depends on the wall tier: Medieval Wood/Stone/Brick = 300/600/1000 HP, Sci-Fi Cement/Iron/Obsidian = 450/900/1500 HP. Upgrading also upgrades existing walls. Walls never catch fire.

[building] Farm
cost: 10 wood
Farm plot (Sci-Fi: Hydro Farm), 10 wood per 1x1 cell on explored open ground. Planting costs 10 food, the wheat grows for about 45 seconds and the harvest returns 30 food (3x the seed, net 2x profit). Plots never run out: after a harvest the plot is empty and can be planted again. Idle workers nearby farm automatically. Build farms when food is low.

[technology] Copper Weapons (Sci-Fi mode name: Meteorite Weapons)
id: WeaponUpgrade1; upgrade line: weapon tier 1
cost: 60 food, 80 gold; research time 20 s at Blacksmith
prerequisite: none
effect: +15% damage for all soldiers (not Workers).
First weapon tier. Starting weapons are Wood (Medieval) / Platinum (Sci-Fi).

[technology] Iron Weapons (Sci-Fi mode name: Obsidian Weapons)
id: WeaponUpgrade2; upgrade line: weapon tier 2
cost: 50 wood, 100 food, 150 gold; research time 30 s at Blacksmith
prerequisite: WeaponUpgrade1 (Copper Weapons)
effect: +30% damage in total for all soldiers.
Second weapon tier.

[technology] Gold Weapons (Sci-Fi mode name: Titanium Weapons)
id: WeaponUpgrade3; upgrade line: weapon tier 3
cost: 100 wood, 150 food, 250 gold; research time 40 s at Blacksmith
prerequisite: WeaponUpgrade2 (Iron Weapons)
effect: +50% damage in total for all soldiers. Maximum weapon tier.
Final weapon tier.

[technology] Wood Armor (Sci-Fi mode name: Platinum Armor)
id: ArmorUpgrade1; upgrade line: armor tier 1
cost: 60 wood, 40 food; research time 15 s at Blacksmith
prerequisite: none
effect: Soldiers take 10% less damage.
First armor tier. Soldiers start with no armor.

[technology] Copper Armor (Sci-Fi mode name: Meteorite Armor)
id: ArmorUpgrade2; upgrade line: armor tier 2
cost: 80 wood, 80 food, 60 gold; research time 25 s at Blacksmith
prerequisite: ArmorUpgrade1
effect: Soldiers take 20% less damage.
Second armor tier.

[technology] Iron Armor (Sci-Fi mode name: Obsidian Armor)
id: ArmorUpgrade3; upgrade line: armor tier 3
cost: 120 wood, 120 food, 140 gold; research time 35 s at Blacksmith
prerequisite: ArmorUpgrade2
effect: Soldiers take 30% less damage.
Third armor tier.

[technology] Gold Armor (Sci-Fi mode name: Titanium Armor)
id: ArmorUpgrade4; upgrade line: armor tier 4
cost: 180 wood, 160 food, 240 gold; research time 45 s at Blacksmith
prerequisite: ArmorUpgrade3
effect: Soldiers take 40% less damage. Maximum armor tier.
Final armor tier.

[technology] Stone Walls (Sci-Fi mode name: Iron Walls)
id: WallUpgrade1; upgrade line: wall tier 1
cost: 100 wood, 50 gold; research time 25 s at Blacksmith
prerequisite: none
effect: Walls become 600 HP (Medieval) / 900 HP (Sci-Fi); existing walls are upgraded too.
First wall tier.

[technology] Brick Walls (Sci-Fi mode name: Obsidian Walls)
id: WallUpgrade2; upgrade line: wall tier 2
cost: 150 wood, 120 gold; research time 35 s at Blacksmith
prerequisite: WallUpgrade1
effect: Walls become 1000 HP (Medieval) / 1500 HP (Sci-Fi). Maximum wall tier.
Final wall tier.

[unit] Worker (Sci-Fi mode name: Engineer)
cost: 50 food; population 1; trained at TownCenter
health 40, damage 3, range 1.0, speed 2.5, vision 5
weak against: Spearman, Archer, Cavalry
Economic unit. Gathers wood, food and gold (carries 10 per trip and drops it at the Town Center), builds every building, plants and harvests farms, works inside a Mine and extinguishes fires. Very weak in combat; keep workers away from enemy soldiers.

[unit] Spearman (Sci-Fi mode name: Marine)
cost: 60 food, 20 gold; population 1; trained at Barracks
health 80, damage 8, range 1.2, speed 2.5, vision 7
strong against (2x damage): Cavalry
weak against: Archer
Low-cost anti-cavalry melee infantry. Deals double (2x) damage to Cavalry (Tank in Sci-Fi mode). Loses to Archers, which outrange it. Best answer when the enemy shows many Cavalry.

[unit] Archer (Sci-Fi mode name: Sniper)
cost: 30 wood, 40 food; population 1; trained at Barracks
health 50, damage 9, range 5.0, speed 2.5, vision 7
strong against (2x damage): Spearman
weak against: Cavalry
Ranged infantry with attack range 5. Deals double (2x) damage to Spearmen (Marines in Sci-Fi). Fragile (50 HP) and countered by fast Cavalry. In Medieval mode only Archers can attack an enemy Archer Tower, and an Archer is the unit that mans your own Archer Tower.

[unit] Cavalry (Sci-Fi mode name: Tank)
cost: 80 food, 40 gold; population 1; trained at Stable
health 100, damage 12, range 1.2, speed 4.5, vision 7
strong against (2x damage): Archer
weak against: Spearman
Fast, durable melee unit (speed 4.5, 100 HP). Deals double (2x) damage to Archers (Snipers in Sci-Fi). Countered by Spearmen. Needs a Stable (Vehicle Bay in Sci-Fi) and gold. In Sci-Fi mode the Tank also fires rockets (2x damage, range 5, reload 2.5 s) and is the only unit that can attack an enemy Rocket Turret.

Counter triangle (both modes). Spearman beats Cavalry, Archer beats Spearman, Cavalry beats Archer. A unit deals 2x damage to the unit type it counters. Sci-Fi names: Marine beats Tank, Sniper beats Marine, Tank beats Sniper. To defend against cavalry/tanks train Spearmen/Marines; against spearmen use Archers; against archers use Cavalry. Mixed armies are safer than a single unit type.

Resources are wood, food and gold. Workers gather from trees (wood), berry bushes and farms (food) and gold deposits (gold), carry up to 10 units per trip and must return them to the Town Center (drop-off) before the resource is added. More workers means faster income. Gold also comes from a Mine (+10 gold every 10 s with one worker inside). Food also comes from farms (harvest returns 3x the food spent planting).

Population: the Town Center gives 25 population capacity and every House (Habitat) adds +5. Every unit costs 1 population, including units waiting in a training queue. If the population limit is reached, training is rejected with "Population limit reached". Build Houses early to avoid blocking production.

Building prerequisites: Workers build every building. Barracks (Armory) is required for Spearman and Archer; Stable (Vehicle Bay) is required for Cavalry/Tank; Blacksmith (Tech Lab) is required for all upgrades; the Town Center trains Workers. A building only works after construction is complete. Each production building has a training queue of at most 5 units, and only one research can run at a time.

Win condition: destroy the opponent's Town Center (Command Center). If your Town Center is destroyed you lose. If the opponent leaves the match, the remaining player wins. After the match both players may vote for a rematch.

Fog of war: a player only sees enemy units and buildings inside the vision radius of their own units and buildings (units 5-7 cells, buildings about 8 cells). Hidden areas show nothing. Enemy resources, enemy technology, enemy economy and enemy units under fog are never visible and cannot be known by the AI advisor. Scouting with a fast unit (Cavalry) reveals more of the map.

Combat: units automatically attack visible enemies in range. Damage = attacker damage x weapon upgrade bonus x 2 if the attacker counters the target, reduced by the target's armor upgrade (10-40%). Units die at 0 HP. Ranged Archers (range 5) can hit melee units before they arrive. Workers are weak (3 damage, 40 HP).

Defense towers: Archer Tower (Medieval) and Rocket Turret (Sci-Fi) cost 100 gold and must be manned by one soldier to fire (Archer in Medieval, Marine in Sci-Fi). Only Archers can damage an enemy Archer Tower, and only Tanks can damage an enemy Rocket Turret. Towers are strong defensive anchors near the base or a gate.

Walls: drawn segment by segment for 10 wood each. Walls block movement and protect workers and buildings. The wall upgrade line (Stone/Brick, or Iron/Obsidian in Sci-Fi) increases the health of all walls.

Upgrades are researched at the Blacksmith (Tech Lab) one at a time. Weapons have 3 tiers (+15%, +30%, +50% damage), Armor has 4 tiers (10%, 20%, 30%, 40% damage reduction), Walls have 2 tiers. Each tier requires the previous tier of the same line. Upgrades affect soldiers only, not Workers. A cancelled research is refunded.

Random disasters hit both sides independently, the computer opponent in single player included. The first one comes 90-150 s into the match, then one every 100-200 s. Fire starts in one of your completed buildings (never in walls) and slowly burns about 10% of your stored wood, food and gold while it burns. Plague lasts 20 seconds and kills 1-3 of your units chosen at random (at least one unit always survives). Rain is only visual and has no gameplay effect.

Fire response: all of your workers automatically stop working and run to the burning building; with at least one worker at the building the fire is out after 12 seconds, without workers it burns out five times slower and keeps burning resources. Firefighting workers cannot take other orders until the fire is out. There is no repair action: if the building is destroyed, rebuild it. Plague response: there is no cure, healing building or quarantine; replace the lost units by training new ones and keep enough workers so the economy recovers.

Economy strategy: keep the Town Center training Workers early, spread workers across wood, food and gold, build Houses before reaching the population cap, add farms for steady food and a Mine for steady gold. Avoid floating unspent resources; spend them on workers, production buildings or upgrades.

Defense strategy: identify the visible enemy unit types first, then train their counter (Spearmen vs Cavalry, Archers vs Spearmen, Cavalry vs Archers). Gather your soldiers near the threatened region, man an Archer Tower / Rocket Turret, and use walls to funnel attackers. Keep workers away from the fight.

Attack strategy: attack when your army is larger or counters the visible enemy army, ideally after a weapon upgrade. Target the enemy Town Center to win. Do not attack blindly into fog: scout first. Bring Archers to destroy an Archer Tower (or Tanks for a Rocket Turret).
